animal head shown frontally (A's top row heads / B's central creature face)
registers or stacked zones of imagery
justification: Both surfaces show animals, humanoid figures and a horizontal band of small repeated motifs, but only at the most generic level: A stacks profile quadrupeds, birds, a snake and small human-like figures in loose registers on a tall vertical field, while B is a strictly mirror-symmetric pair of frontal costumed figures holding rattles and flanking a central vertical band topped by an animal mask, centred on a rayed disc. Nothing distinctive is shared — no matching posture, attribute, or specific pairing — and the conventions differ sharply (spare schematic profile relief versus bold outlined, polychrome, frontal, heavily patterned figures).
